newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian manufacturers see weaker GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Australian manufacturers see weaker GDP growth.

text.p: The Australian Chamber of Manufactures (ACM) on Thursday said gross domestic product (GDP) growth for 1996/97 (July-June) is likely to ease to 2.7 percent as conditions for a recovery in manufacturing remain fragile.
The Federal Government is forecasting 1996/97 GDP growth of 3.25 percent.
The ACM said its June quarter survey of 646 companies showed manufacturing trends for the quarter were marginally positive but growth was patchy.
Companies reporting increased production narrowly outnumbered those showing a decrease, but gains outnumbered declines in only six of the 12 manufacturing sectors.
Manufacturing product declined 0.1 percent for the June quarter, following declines of 0.2 percent, 0.6 percent and 0.6 percent in the previous three quarters.
"Manufacturing product has now fallen by 1.1 percent in the past 12 months. On this basis, GDP growth for 1996/97 is likely to slip to about 2.7 percent," the ACM said.
Acting chief executive Richard Seddon said the outlook was for a modest improvement in production, sales, exports and profits, but added employment prospects remained weak.
"While there are some signs of growth and September quarter expectations are positive, the improvement is coming off a very low base and is very subdued," Seddon said in a statement.
"Manufacturing is likely to take at least another quarter or two to make up lost ground and move into a stronger growth phase."
